Because the very character of ORV inserts into the ambience of other nearby persons a variety of environmental effects (such as the sight and sound of a mechanical intrusion), it follows that their presence on areas designated to preserve the natural milieu would be contrary to the basic purposes of such areas; natural areas of the National Park System and of the National Wildlife Refuge System are lands under jurisdiction of the Department which would have their basic program missions compromised if ORV use were permitted on them.
Delegate to Bureaus the Authority to Implement the Executive Order Without Secretarial Review:
In accord with their respective program responsibilities, the Department's bureaus have already taken some measures to manage ORV use on their respective lands. Selection of this alternative would result in the following impacts:
Such delegation of Secretarial authority would continue the situation whereby the rules and regulations on lands administered by Bureaus within the Department are different, resulting in confusion among ORV users and among those who object to their presence on the public lands.
It would result in about the same nature and extent of environmental impacts as the proposed action.
